housing.summary: New York City has an extremely competitive and expensive rental market, especially in Manhattan. Leases usually require proof of income (often 40x monthly rent), credit check, and sometimes a guarantor for newcomers without US credit history.

banking.summary: Opening a US bank account typically requires a Social Security Number (SSN) or ITIN, a passport, and proof of a US address. Major national banks have extensive branch networks across NYC.

schools.summary: New York City operates the largest public school system in the US via the NYC Department of Education, alongside numerous private and international schools offering IB and other curricula.

legal_admin.summary: The US has no local residence registration system. New arrivals enter on a visa with an I-94 admission record and must apply for a Social Security Number if authorized to work.
legal_admin.registration_step: Apply for a Social Security Number (SSN) after arrival if work-authorized

tax_finance.summary: US federal income tax is administered by the IRS. Residents need a Social Security Number (SSN) or, if ineligible, an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) to file. New York State and New York City also levy income taxes.

transport.summary: New York City's public transit is run by the MTA, including the 24-hour subway and extensive bus network. Fares use the OMNY contactless system or MetroCard. Newcomers may exchange or apply for a driver's license through the NY DMV. There is no universal public healthcare registration; coverage is via employer or private insurance.
transport.network_name: MTA (New York City Subway and Buses)
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Foreign drivers must apply for a NY State license through the NY DMV; no reciprocal exchange for most countries, road/knowledge tests may be required
transport.healthcare_registration: No universal registration; coverage via employer-sponsored or private health insurance
